item: R5 - a real pre-takeover client calling the taken-over service, over the wire, in an isolated environment
goal_text_being_satisfied: _agent/ani-governance-tx7do-plan/goals/T15.md: at least one legacy-client to new-service HTTP or gRPC contract and error comparison; this does not substitute a descriptor diff or a new-client self-test

environment.service: app/admin/service/cmd/server built from 10f8577, started as a separate process on 127.0.0.1:17788 (SSE 17789) with a task-private config directory copied from app/admin/service/configs and rewritten for the task: database name, redis address, ports
environment.database: task-named disposable database tx7do_t15_r5 inside the already authorized task container tx7do-t07-acc-lab-pg; schema applied by running the seven committed migrations/ files in filename order because Atlas is not installed on this host; the service itself ran with migrate: false, unchanged
environment.seed: one-time `admin init --username admin --password-file <task file>` against that database: 'PASS: initial seed and administrator committed', then `admin check`: 'PASS: platform administrator and required API grants are present' (1 user, 213 registered API rows)
environment.redis: container ani-governance-t11-redis started and stopped by scripts/verify-gpu-redis.sh for this round only
environment.secret_material: ANI_ACCESS_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE pointed at a task-private 64-hex key file; the administrator password lives only in the task directory; nothing was written outside it
environment.isolation: no business DSN exists on this host and none was used; the gate's gov_acc_data / gov_acc_lab databases were left running and untouched, verified after teardown

legacy_client.source_tree: the frozen pre-takeover baseline d27847b99479553b1a56fc84bc4ee8f1a0992e1e, exported with git archive into /home/ubuntu/tx7do-pilot-run/T15/r5/legacy (no checkout, the working repository was not switched)
legacy_client.client_library: api/gen/go at that commit, exactly as the takeover found it: go-wind-admin/api/gen/go/admin/service/v1 HTTP clients plus go-wind-admin/api/gen/go/identity/service/v1 messages
legacy_client.upstream_links_measured: go version -m of the legacy probe binary reports dep github.com/tx7do/go-crud/api v0.0.7 and dep github.com/tx7do/go-wind-toolkit/protoc-gen-go-redact v0.0.0-20260831125122-5bb4931991b2
legacy_client.current_client: the identical probe source compiled in a detached worktree of 10f8577, whose pagination messages come from go-wind-admin/pkg/localdeps/go-crud/...; go version -m of that binary reports zero github.com/tx7do modules
legacy_client.source_identity: probe main.go is byte-identical between the two trees (cmp verified); only a six-line shim differs, because the pagination import path is the thing under test

cases_and_results.run_both: each case executed twice, once per client binary, against the same live service; logs /home/ubuntu/tx7do-pilot-run/T15/r5/evidence/probe-{legacy,new}.txt
cases_and_results.identical: 14 of 14 after normalizing exactly three run-specific values: the server's request_id in error metadata, the random username suffix the probe generates, and the database auto-increment id of the row it created. Raw error strings compare equal once only the request id is normalized.

contracts_exercised.auth: PlatformPasswordLogin returned a 791-character token, expires_in 5400, issued_at present
contracts_exercised.paging: List through the pagination message of each tree: total 1, page/limit/order_by honoured, item fields parsed
contracts_exercised.partial_update_with_mask: Update with update_mask=['nickname'] changed nickname and left email, mobile, username and tenant_id untouched (verified by reading back)
contracts_exercised.validation_error: Update without the required relation returned 400 BAD_REQUEST 'role_ids is required'
contracts_exercised.permission_error: the same List with no credential returned 401 UNAUTHORIZED 'missing bearer token'
contracts_exercised.not_found: Get of an unused id returned code 500 with message 'ent: user not found' and an empty reason
contracts_exercised.tenant_scope: UserExists by username without a tenant scope returned 400 'tenant scope required to check user exists by username'
contracts_exercised.redaction: a created user with mobile 13800001234 read back as '138****1234' while email came back intact; the legacy client parsed the masked value and reported mobile_equal=false, email_equal=true, i.e. the masking is the server's and the old client reads it the same way the new one does
contracts_exercised.cleanup: the created user was deleted through the client; sys_users then held 1 row, 1 live

findings_registered_not_changed: docs/interface-integration-register.md carries the three interface observations from this run (not-found surfacing as 500 with an empty reason, username existence checks requiring tenant scope, mobile masked while email is not). None was repaired here: the task is takeover equivalence, the behaviour is identical on both sides of the takeover, and changing an error mapping would be a business change outside this plan.
not_covered_by_this_item: gRPC was not compared: this service configuration exposes the HTTP REST server, the SSE server and the asynq queue, and no gRPC listener is configured, so there is no gRPC contract to call here
integration with a real external client application (a browser or third-party caller outside this repository) was not executed; that stays listed as not_verified and is not implied by these results
multi-service acceptance (Network, accelerator downstream) is unchanged from its earlier scope
tenant-cross isolation and quota enforcement semantics are covered by the quota gates, not by this probe

resource_teardown.done: server process terminated (ports 17788/17789 show zero listeners), this round's redis container removed by the same script that created it, task database tx7do_t15_r5 dropped (present: 0), the two r5 worktrees removed, repository tree clean
resource_teardown.mistake_recorded: the first teardown pass reported success for later stages but had not stopped the service: it read a stale pid file, because the server had been restarted from a different shell after the pid was written, and DROP DATABASE then failed with 'being accessed by other users'. This was caught by re-checking the port and the database rather than trusting the script, and the corrected termination and drop are appended to /home/ubuntu/tx7do-pilot-run/T15/r5/evidence/drop-task-db.log.
resource_teardown.left_alone_deliberately: container tx7do-t04-captcha-redis is up but belongs to an earlier round and not to this script's container name (ani-governance-t11-redis), so it was identified and left for its owner rather than removed by this round
resource_teardown.intact: gov_acc_dev, gov_acc_joint_b, gov_acc_test_owner, gov_acc_data and gov_acc_lab all still present; guard and lab containers untouched
